'''''Lithothamnion''''' is a genus of thalloid [[Red algae|red alga]] comprising 103 species. Its members are known by a number of common names.<ref group=note>Recorded common names are griuán, maërl, punalevä-suku, stenhinna and maerl.</ref> The monomerous, crustose thalli are composed of a single system of filaments which grow close to the underlying surface. ''Lithothamnion'' reproduces by means of multiporate [[conceptacle]]s.

== Uses ==
[[File:Vegan calcium supplements.jpg|thumb|Calcium supplements made from ''Lithothamnium calcareum'']]
The species ''Lithothamnium calcareum'' is, besides [[Tricalcium phosphate]], often used as [[food fortification]] in [[plant-based diet|plant-based]] [[milk substitute]]s to achieve a similar [[calcium]] content as a [[cow milk]] which is around 120 mg/100 ml.<ref>{{Citation |editor-last=Klapp |editor-first=Anna-Lena |date=October 2019 |title=The Plant Milk Report |publisher=[[ProVeg International|ProVeg]] e. V. |publication-place=Berlin |isbn=978-3-948516-00-0 |page=16 |chapter=OTHER PLANT MILKS |chapter-url=https://proveg.com/plant-based-food-and-lifestyle/vegan-alternatives/plant-milk-report/ |access-date=2021-03-02}} </ref>  However, in April 2021 the [[European Court of Justice]] forbade its use in [[organic food]] products such as drinks.<ref>[https://www.courthousenews.com/eu-court-forbids-calcium-sourced-from-algae-in-organic-drinks/ EU Court Forbids Calcium Sourced From Algae in Organic Drinks] ([https://www.courthousenews.com/ Courthouse News Service])</ref><ref>[https://www.natlawreview.com/article/important-european-court-justice-decision-adding-non-organic-ingredients-to-organic Important European Court of Justice decision on adding non-organic ingredients to organic drinks] ([https://www.natlawreview.com/ The National Law Review])</ref><ref>[https://curia.europa.eu/jcms/upload/docs/application/pdf/2021-04/cp210069en.pdf EU law prohibits the addition of the alga Lithothamnium calcareum in the processing of organic foodstuffs for the purpose of their enrichment with calcium (Case C-815/19)] ([http://curia.europa.eu/ ECJ])</ref><ref>[http://curia.europa.eu/juris/documents.jsf?num=C-815/19 Full text of judgment in case C-815/19 (ECJ)]</ref>
